doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Earliest memories of singing in the living room
summary: She recalls singing pop songs like I'll Walk Alone and My Little Margie, doing a soft shoe for the family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I read somewhere a reference to I’ll Walk Alone? Is that a hymn? Or is that a – does that ring any bells for you? A song that you sang at age . . .
“I’ll walk alone, because to tell you the truth, I’ll be lonely.” It wasn’t – that wasn’t a religious song. It was a popular – called the pop of the day, I guess.
Are your earliest memories of singing church or other, and what other?
My earliest memories of singing are doing the soft shoe and singing My Little Margie.
Yeah, and they had to pay attention. I told you I was a showoff, and everybody would want to hear the little kid sing. So it worked out fine.
